identity.title: Antitumor properties of novel sesquiterpene lactone analogs as NFkappaB inhibitors that bind to the IKKbeta ubiquitin-like domain (ULD).

content.abstract: Melampomagnolide B (MMB, 3) is a parthenolide (PTL, 1) based sesquiterpene lactone that has been used as a template for the synthesis of a plethora of lead anticancer agents owing to its reactive C-10 primary hydroxyl group. Such compounds have been shown to inhibit the IKKbeta subunit, preventing phosphorylation of the cytoplasmic IkappaB inhibitory complex. The present study focuses on the synthesis and in vitro antitumor properties of novel benzyl and phenethyl carbamates of MMB (7a-7k). Screening of these MMB carbamates identified analogs with potent growth inhibition properties against a panel of 60 human cancer cell lines (71% of the molecules screened had GI(50) values < 2 muM). Two analogs, the benzyl carbamate 7b and the phenethyl carbamate7k, were the most active compounds. Lead compound 7b inhibited cell proliferation in M9 ENL AML cells, and in TMD-231, OV-MD-231 and SUM149 breast cancer cell lines. Interestingly, mechanistic studies showed that 7b did not inhibit p65 phosphorylation in M9 ENL AML and OV-MD-231 cells, but did inhibit phophorylation of both p65 and IkappaBalpha in SUM149 cells. 7b also reduced NFkappaB binding to DNA in both OV-MD-231 and SUM149 cells. Molecular docking studies indicated that 7b and 7k are both predicted to interact with the ubiquitin-like domain (ULD) of the IKKbeta subunit. These data suggest that in SUM149 cells, 7b is likely acting as an allosteric inhibitor of IKKbeta, whereas in M9 ENL AML and OV-MD-231 cells 7b is able to inhibit an event after IkappaB/p65/p50 phosphorylation by IKKbeta that leads to inhibition of NFkappaB activation and reduction in NFkappaB-DNA binding. Analog 7b was by far the most potent compound in either carbamate series, and was considered an important lead compound for further optimization and development as an anticancer agent.
